symbols.name: S
symbols.def: baseline-stratum index set

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: stage index set

symbols.name: I
symbols.def: the admissible holdout fractions

symbols.name: mtr
symbols.def: \(m_{nks}=\lfloor N_{nks}/2\rfloor\) is the prespecified treated quota in stage--stratum block \((k,s)\).

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: \(h=(h_s)_{s\in S}\) is the local additive-effect coordinate.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: \(B_n\) is the fixed baseline-outcome triangular array.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: For every \(h\in H\cup\{0\}\), \(Y^{(h)}_{nksi}(0)=B_{nksi}\) and \(Y^{(h)}_{nksi}(1)=B_{nksi}+h_s/\sqrt n\). At \(h=0\), this construction is the prespecified Fisher sharp-zero array.

symbols.name: tau
symbols.def: \(\tau^{(h)}_{n,s}=N_{n\cdot s}^{-1}\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{i\le N_{nks}}\{Y^{(h)}_{nksi}(1)-Y^{(h)}_{nksi}(0)\}=h_s/\sqrt n\)

symbols.name: Kpair
symbols.def: For \(u>0\), \(K_{nks}(u)=\sum_{i,l}\{\mathbf 1[0<B_{nksl}-B_{nksi}<u]+\tfrac12\mathbf 1[B_{nksl}-B_{nksi}=0]+\tfrac12\mathbf 1[B_{nksl}-B_{nksi}=u]\}\), and \(K_{nks}(0)=0\). This is the exact ordered-pair crossing-count convention for baseline midranks.

symbols.name: U0
symbols.def: \(U^0_{nksi}=N_{nks}^{-1}\{\sum_{l=1}^{N_{nks}}\mathbf 1[B_{nksl}<B_{nksi}]+\tfrac12\sum_{l=1}^{N_{nks}}\mathbf 1[B_{nksl}=B_{nksi}]\}\) is the normalized baseline midrank.

symbols.name: lambda
symbols.def: \(\lambda_{ks}\) is the coefficient in the uniform limit \(N_{nks}^{-3/2}K_{nks}(u/\sqrt{N_{nks}})\to\lambda_{ks}u\) on the declared compact \(u\)-window.

symbols.name: rshare
symbols.def: \(r_{ks}=\lim_{n\to\infty}N_{nks}/n\)

symbols.name: Z1
symbols.def: \(Z_{n1si}\) is drawn at stage 1 before recruitment, with exactly \(m_{n1s}\) treated units in stratum \(s\).

symbols.name: rg
symbols.def: \(r_{\mathrm g}\) is the generic correlation argument of the selected-score quantile.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: Let \(G_{ns}(\rho)=\{1,\ldots,N_{n1s}\}\setminus H_{n,s}(\rho)\), \(g^z_{ns}=\sum_{i\in G_{ns}(\rho)}\mathbf 1\{Z_{n1si}=z\}\), \(\bar Y^z_{G,ns}=(g^z_{ns})^{-1}\sum_{i\in G_{ns}(\rho)}\mathbf 1\{Z_{n1si}=z\}Y^{\mathrm{obs},1}_{nsi}\), and \(s^{2,z}_{G,ns}=(g^z_{ns}-1)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G_{ns}(\rho)}\mathbf 1\{Z_{n1si}=z\}(Y^{\mathrm{obs},1}_{nsi}-\bar Y^z_{G,ns})^2\). When \(g^0_{ns},g^1_{ns}\ge2\) and \(\widehat v^X_{ns}=s^{2,1}_{G,ns}/g^1_{ns}+s^{2,0}_{G,ns}/g^0_{ns}>0\), define the uncentered selector \(X_{n,s}(\rho)=(\bar Y^1_{G,ns}-\bar Y^0_{G,ns})/\sqrt{\widehat v^X_{ns}}\); otherwise set \(X_{n,s}(\rho)=c_s-1\), which deterministically means no recruitment.

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: a deterministic two-stratum recruitment label, with \(C_s=1\) meaning that stratum \(s\) is recruited

symbols.name: Cn
symbols.def: \(C_n(\rho)=(\mathbf{1}\{X_{n,s}(\rho)>c_s\}:s\in S)\)

symbols.name: Hist1
symbols.def: \(\mathcal F_{n,1}(\rho)=\sigma\{H_{n,t}(\rho),Z_{n1ti},Y^{\mathrm{obs},1}_{nti},X_{n,t}(\rho),C_n(\rho):t\in S,i\le N_{n1t}\}\) is the realized history after stage-1 assignment and recruitment and before stage-2 assignment.

symbols.name: Z2
symbols.def: \(Z_{n2si}\) exists only for a recruited stratum and is drawn after \(\mathcal F_{n,1}(\rho)\), with exactly \(m_{n2s}\) treated units.

symbols.name: Dobs
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}=(H_{n,s}(\rho),Z_{n1s},Y^{\mathrm{obs},1}_{ns},C_n(\rho),(Z_{n2s},Y^{\mathrm{obs},2}_{ns})_{s:C_{n,s}(\rho)=1})_{s\in S}\) is the chronologically observed dataset.
symbols.role: realized alternative dataset at holdout fraction \(\rho\)

symbols.name: YF
symbols.def: For every unit observed in \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\), the Fisher completion indexed by the same design value sets \(\widetilde Y^{0,\mathcal D(\rho)}_{nksi}(0)=\widetilde Y^{0,\mathcal D(\rho)}_{nksi}(1)=Y^{\mathrm{obs},k}_{nsi}\); no equality between \(Y^{(h)}(1)\) and \(Y^{(h)}(0)\) is imposed when \(h\ne0\).
symbols.role: sharp-null completion used only by rerandomization

symbols.name: Omega1
symbols.def: \(\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)=\{(H'_{n,s},z'_{n1s}):H'_{n,s}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N_{n1s}\},\ |H'_{n,s}|=\lfloor\rho N_{n1s}\rfloor,\ z'_{n1s}\in\{0,1\}^{N_{n1s}},\ \sum_i z'_{n1si}=m_{n1s}\}\). Under the pre-cell candidate law, each element has mass \(\{\binom{N_{n1s}}{\lfloor\rho N_{n1s}\rfloor}\binom{N_{n1s}}{m_{n1s}}\}^{-1}\), independently across \(s\in S\).

symbols.name: Xprime
symbols.def: For \((H'_{n,s},z'_{n1s})\in\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)\), let \(G'_s=\{1,\ldots,N_{n1s}\}\setminus H'_{n,s}\), \(g_s^{\prime z}=\sum_{i\in G'_s}\mathbf 1\{z'_{n1si}=z\}\), \(\bar Y_{G,s}^{\prime z}=(g_s^{\prime z})^{-1}\sum_{i\in G'_s}\mathbf 1\{z'_{n1si}=z\}\widetilde Y^{0,\mathcal D(\rho)}_{n1si}\), and \(s_{G,s}^{\prime2,z}=(g_s^{\prime z}-1)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G'_s}\mathbf 1\{z'_{n1si}=z\}(\widetilde Y^{0,\mathcal D(\rho)}_{n1si}-\bar Y_{G,s}^{\prime z})^2\). If \(g_s^{\prime0},g_s^{\prime1}\ge2\) and \(\widehat v_{ns}^{X\prime}=s_{G,s}^{\prime2,1}/g_s^{\prime1}+s_{G,s}^{\prime2,0}/g_s^{\prime0}>0\), set \(X'_{n,s}=(\bar Y_{G,s}^{\prime1}-\bar Y_{G,s}^{\prime0})/\sqrt{\widehat v_{ns}^{X\prime}}\); otherwise set \(X'_{n,s}=c_s-1\).
symbols.role: Fisher-completed selector recomputed for every stage-1 candidate

symbols.name: Cprime
symbols.def: For a candidate \(((H'_{n,s},z'_{n1s}))_{s\in S}\in\prod_{s\in S}\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)\), \(C'_n(\rho)=(\mathbf 1\{X'_{n,s}>c_s\}:s\in S)\).

symbols.name: OmegaC
symbols.def: \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\) contains exactly the histories \(((H'_{n,s},z'_{n1s})_{s\in S},(z'_{n2s})_{s:C_s=1})\) such that \((H'_{n,s},z'_{n1s})\in\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)\), \(C'_n(\rho)=C_n(\rho)=C\), and \(z'_{n2s}\in\{0,1\}^{N_{n2s}}\) with \(\sum_i z'_{n2si}=m_{n2s}\) for every retained stratum \(s\) satisfying \(C_s=1\). There is no stage-2 coordinate when \(C_s=0\).

symbols.name: Pn
symbols.def: \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) is the sampling law for the fixed array \(B_n\): draw the independent simple-random holdouts, then the two independent stratumwise stage-1 complete randomizations, observe responses from \(Y^{(h)}\), realize \(C_n(\rho)\), and finally draw independent stage-2 complete randomizations only in recruited strata conditional on \(\mathcal F_{n,1}(\rho)\).
symbols.role: chronological local-alternative sampling law at holdout fraction \(\rho\)

symbols.name: Rbase
symbols.def: Given \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\), \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,\mathrm{base}}\) is the stage-1 candidate law that assigns independently across strata mass \(\prod_{s\in S}\{\binom{N_{n1s}}{\lfloor\rho N_{n1s}\rfloor}\binom{N_{n1s}}{m_{n1s}}\}^{-1}\) to every element of \(\prod_{s\in S}\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)\), then recomputes \(X'_{n,s}\) and \(C'_n(\rho)\) from \(\widetilde Y^{0,\mathcal D(\rho)}\). It generates no stage-2 assignment before the candidate cell is retained.
symbols.role: explicit pre-cell stage-1 Fisher candidate law

symbols.name: EC
symbols.def: \(E_{n,C}(\rho)=\{C_n(\rho)=C\}=\bigcap_{t\in S:C_t=1}\{X_{n,t}(\rho)>c_t\}\cap\bigcap_{t\in S:C_t=0}\{X_{n,t}(\rho)\le c_t\}\)

symbols.name: prefcell
symbols.def: \(p_{\mathrm{ref}}(n,C,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)=\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,\mathrm{base}}\{C'_n(\rho)=C\}\) equals the sum, over all \(((H'_{n,s},z'_{n1s}))_{s\in S}\in\prod_{s\in S}\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)\) with \(C'_n(\rho)=C\), of \(\prod_{s\in S}\{\binom{N_{n1s}}{\lfloor\rho N_{n1s}\rfloor}\binom{N_{n1s}}{m_{n1s}}\}^{-1}\).

symbols.name: J
symbols.def: the fixed nonempty set of retained active cell--stratum pairs; inactive pairs with \(C_s=0\) are never tested

symbols.name: R1
symbols.def: For \(j=(C,s)\in J\), set \(U^{\mathrm{obs},1}_{nsi}=N_{n1s}^{-1}\{\sum_l\mathbf 1[Y^{\mathrm{obs},1}_{nsl}<Y^{\mathrm{obs},1}_{nsi}]+\tfrac12\sum_l\mathbf 1[Y^{\mathrm{obs},1}_{nsl}=Y^{\mathrm{obs},1}_{nsi}]\}\), \(\bar U^{\mathrm{obs},1}_{ns}=N_{n1s}^{-1}\sum_iU^{\mathrm{obs},1}_{nsi}\), and \(S^{2,U}_{n1s}=(N_{n1s}-1)^{-1}\sum_i(U^{\mathrm{obs},1}_{nsi}-\bar U^{\mathrm{obs},1}_{ns})^2\). When \(1\le m_{n1s}<N_{n1s}\) and \(S^{2,U}_{n1s}>0\), let \(D^R_{n1s}=m_{n1s}^{-1}\sum_iZ_{n1si}U^{\mathrm{obs},1}_{nsi}-(N_{n1s}-m_{n1s})^{-1}\sum_i(1-Z_{n1si})U^{\mathrm{obs},1}_{nsi}\), \(\widehat v^R_{n1s}=S^{2,U}_{n1s}\{m_{n1s}^{-1}+(N_{n1s}-m_{n1s})^{-1}\}\), and \(R_{1j}=D^R_{n1s}/\sqrt{\widehat v^R_{n1s}}\); otherwise set \(R_{1j}=0\).

symbols.name: R2
symbols.def: For active \(j=(C,s)\in J\), set \(U^{\mathrm{obs},2}_{nsi}=N_{n2s}^{-1}\{\sum_l\mathbf 1[Y^{\mathrm{obs},2}_{nsl}<Y^{\mathrm{obs},2}_{nsi}]+\tfrac12\sum_l\mathbf 1[Y^{\mathrm{obs},2}_{nsl}=Y^{\mathrm{obs},2}_{nsi}]\}\), \(\bar U^{\mathrm{obs},2}_{ns}=N_{n2s}^{-1}\sum_iU^{\mathrm{obs},2}_{nsi}\), and \(S^{2,U}_{n2s}=(N_{n2s}-1)^{-1}\sum_i(U^{\mathrm{obs},2}_{nsi}-\bar U^{\mathrm{obs},2}_{ns})^2\). When \(1\le m_{n2s}<N_{n2s}\) and \(S^{2,U}_{n2s}>0\), let \(D^R_{n2s}=m_{n2s}^{-1}\sum_iZ_{n2si}U^{\mathrm{obs},2}_{nsi}-(N_{n2s}-m_{n2s})^{-1}\sum_i(1-Z_{n2si})U^{\mathrm{obs},2}_{nsi}\), \(\widehat v^R_{n2s}=S^{2,U}_{n2s}\{m_{n2s}^{-1}+(N_{n2s}-m_{n2s})^{-1}\}\), and \(R_{2j}=D^R_{n2s}/\sqrt{\widehat v^R_{n2s}}\); otherwise set \(R_{2j}=0\).

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: \(T_j(\theta_j)=\cos(\theta_j)R_{1j}+\sin(\theta_j)R_{2j}\)

symbols.name: Rprime
symbols.def: For a history in \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\), stage \(k\), and \(j=(C,s)\in J\), set \(U'_{nksi}=N_{nks}^{-1}\{\sum_l\mathbf 1[\widetilde Y^{0,\mathcal D(\rho)}_{nksl}<\widetilde Y^{0,\mathcal D(\rho)}_{nksi}]+\tfrac12\sum_l\mathbf 1[\widetilde Y^{0,\mathcal D(\rho)}_{nksl}=\widetilde Y^{0,\mathcal D(\rho)}_{nksi}]\}\), \(\bar U'_{nks}=N_{nks}^{-1}\sum_iU'_{nksi}\), and \(S_{nks}^{\prime2,U}=(N_{nks}-1)^{-1}\sum_i(U'_{nksi}-\bar U'_{nks})^2\). With the candidate assignment \(z'_{nks}\), define \(D_{nks}^{R\prime}=m_{nks}^{-1}\sum_i z'_{nksi}U'_{nksi}-(N_{nks}-m_{nks})^{-1}\sum_i(1-z'_{nksi})U'_{nksi}\), \(\widehat v_{nks}^{R\prime}=S_{nks}^{\prime2,U}\{m_{nks}^{-1}+(N_{nks}-m_{nks})^{-1}\}\), and \(R'_{kj}=D_{nks}^{R\prime}/\sqrt{\widehat v_{nks}^{R\prime}}\) when the quotas and variance are nondegenerate; otherwise set \(R'_{kj}=0\).

symbols.name: Tprime
symbols.def: \(T'_j(\theta_j)=\cos(\theta_j)R'_{1j}+\sin(\theta_j)R'_{2j}\) for each supported candidate history and active \(j\in J\).
symbols.role: recomputed weighted statistic under the Fisher reference

symbols.name: Pref
symbols.def: When \(p_{\mathrm{ref}}(n,C,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)>0\), first restrict and normalize \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,\mathrm{base}}\) on \(C'_n(\rho)=C_n(\rho)=C\), then independently draw each quota-respecting \(z'_{n2s}\) only for \(C_s=1\). The resulting \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,C}\) has support exactly \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\); each supported history has mass \(p_{\mathrm{ref}}(n,C,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)^{-1}\prod_{s\in S}\{\binom{N_{n1s}}{\lfloor\rho N_{n1s}\rfloor}\binom{N_{n1s}}{m_{n1s}}\}^{-1}\prod_{s:C_s=1}\binom{N_{n2s}}{m_{n2s}}^{-1}\), and its statistic is \(T'_j(\theta_j)\).
symbols.role: explicit same-cell Fisher sharp-null chronological reference

symbols.name: phi
symbols.def: standard normal density

symbols.name: Phi
symbols.def: standard normal distribution function

symbols.name: b1
symbols.def: For \(j=(C,s)\in J\), define \(b_{1j}=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sqrt3K_{n1s}(h_s/\sqrt n)/(h_sN_{n1s}^{3/2})=\sqrt3\lambda_{1s}\sqrt{r_{1s}}\), using the exact crossing count that generates the local mean of \(R_{1j}\).

symbols.name: b2
symbols.def: For \(j=(C,s)\in J\), define \(b_{2j}=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sqrt3K_{n2s}(h_s/\sqrt n)/(h_sN_{n2s}^{3/2})=\sqrt3\lambda_{2s}\sqrt{r_{2s}}\), using the exact crossing count that generates the local mean of \(R_{2j}\).

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.def: For \(j=(C,s)\in J\), define \(\kappa_j=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\sum_i(B_{n1si}-\bar B_{n1s})(U^0_{n1si}-\bar U^0_{n1s})}{[\sum_i(B_{n1si}-\bar B_{n1s})^2\sum_i(U^0_{n1si}-\bar U^0_{n1s})^2]^{1/2}}\), where the bars are block averages.

symbols.name: Delta
symbols.def: For \(j=(C,s)\in J\), \(\Delta_j=A_s-\kappa_j b_{1j}\)

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: For \(j=(C,s)\in J\), \(a_j(\rho)=A_s\sqrt{1-\rho}\)

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: \(r_j(\rho,\theta_j)=\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho}\cos(\theta_j)\)

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: \(d_j(\theta_j)=b_{1j}\cos(\theta_j)+b_{2j}\sin(\theta_j)\)

symbols.name: v
symbols.def: \(v_j(\rho,\theta_j)=\sqrt{1-r_j(\rho,\theta_j)^2}\)

symbols.name: qbeta
symbols.def: \(q_{\beta}(r_{\mathrm g},x)\) is the unique \(q\) satisfying \(\Pr\{r_{\mathrm g}Z+\sqrt{1-r_{\mathrm g}^2}E>q\mid Z>x\}=\beta\) for independent standard normal \(Z,E\).

symbols.name: Eq
symbols.def: For \(0<t<1\), \(\operatorname{Eq}_{\beta,r}(c_0,c_1;t)\) means \(q_{\beta}(r,(1-t)c_0+tc_1)=(1-t)q_{\beta}(r,c_0)+tq_{\beta}(r,c_1)\).

symbols.name: qalpha
symbols.def: For \(j=(C,s)\in J\), \(q_{\alpha,j}(\rho,\theta_j)\) is the unique \(q\) satisfying \(\int_{c_s}^{\infty}\phi(z)Q((q-r_j(\rho,\theta_j)z)/v_j(\rho,\theta_j))\,dz=\alpha Q(c_s)\); this is the active-stratum null quantile after conditioning on the full event \(E_{n,C}(\rho)\)

symbols.name: Pi
symbols.def: For \(j=(C,s)\in J\), \(\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,h_s)=Q(c_s-a_j(\rho)h_s)^{-1}\int_{c_s-a_j(\rho)h_s}^{\infty}\phi(z)Q((q_{\alpha,j}(\rho,\theta_j)-d_j(\theta_j)h_s-r_j(\rho,\theta_j)z)/v_j(\rho,\theta_j))\,dz\); this is power conditional on the complete signed event \(E_{n,C}(\rho)\)

symbols.name: Gshift
symbols.def: \(G^h_j(x;\rho,\theta_j)\) is the cdf of \(T_j(\theta_j)\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}gaussian\mbox{-}experiment}\) with drift \(h_s\), conditional on its complete signed cell \(E_C\).

symbols.name: Gzero
symbols.def: \(G^0_j(x;\rho,\theta_j)\) is the same complete-cell conditional Gaussian cdf with every drift set to zero; its upper \(\alpha\)-quantile is \(q_{\alpha,j}(\rho,\theta_j)\).

symbols.name: ell
symbols.def: \(\ell_s=\min\{h_s:h\in H\}\)

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: \(M_j(\rho)=\max_{\vartheta\in[0,\pi/2]}\Pi_j(\rho,\vartheta,\ell_s)\) for \(j=(C,s)\)

symbols.name: F
symbols.def: \(F(\rho)=\min_{j\in J}M_j(\rho)\)

symbols.name: Vstar
symbols.def: \(V^{\star}=\max_{\rho\in I}F(\rho)\)

symbols.name: Sstar
symbols.def: \(\mathcal{S}^{\star}=\{(\rho,(\theta_j)_{j\in J}):\min_{j\in J}\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,\ell_s)=V^{\star}\}\)

symbols.name: M4
symbols.def: \(M_4\) is the uniform empirical centered fourth-moment bound for the baseline blocks.

symbols.name: eta
symbols.def: For each admissible fixed baseline array \(B=(B_n)_n\), \(\eta_n(B)\downarrow0\) is an array-dependent common approximation remainder derived in \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}selected\mbox{-}transfer}\).

symbols.name: dsamp
symbols.def: \(d^{\mathrm{samp}}_n(B)\) is the supremum over active \(j=(C,s)\in J\), \(\rho\in I\), \(\theta\in[0,\pi/2]^J\), \(h\in H\), and \(x\in\mathbb R\) of \(\lvert\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{T_j(\theta_j)\le x\mid E_{n,C}(\rho)\}-G^h_j(x;\rho,\theta_j)\rvert\).

symbols.name: Fref
symbols.def: For \(j=(C,s)\in J\), \(F^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,j}(x;\rho,\theta_j,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})=\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,C}\{T'_j(\theta_j)\le x\}\) is the Fisher-reference cdf built from the dataset realized under \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) at that same \(\rho\).

symbols.name: qrefn
symbols.def: \(q^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,j}(\rho,\theta_j,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})=\inf\{x:F^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,j}(x;\rho,\theta_j,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})\ge1-\alpha\}\) is the upper \(\alpha\)-critical value of the same \(\rho\)-indexed Fisher-reference cdf.

symbols.name: dref
symbols.def: For a dataset \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\) realized at a fixed \(\rho\), \(d^{\mathrm{ref}}_n(B,\rho,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})=\sup_{j=(C,s)\in J,\,\theta\in[0,\pi/2]^J,\,x\in\mathbb R}\max\{\lvert F^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,j}(x;\rho,\theta_j,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})-G^0_j(x;\rho,\theta_j)\rvert,\lvert q^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,j}(\rho,\theta_j,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})-q_{\alpha,j}(\rho,\theta_j)\rvert\}\).

symbols.name: Wmix
symbols.def: the deterministic-quantile two-component-uniform baseline schedule specified in \(\mathrm{def{:}negative\mbox{-}mixture\mbox{-}witness}\), with local outcomes generated from it by \(Y^{(h)}(0)=B\) and \(Y^{(h)}(1)=B+h_s/\sqrt n\)

assumptions.condition: Each \(Y^{(h)}_{nksi}(z)\) depends only on unit \(i\)'s own treatment \(z\).

After the holdouts are drawn and before recruitment is evaluated, \(\mathcal L((Z_{n1s})_{s\in S}\mid(H_{n,s}(\rho))_{s\in S})=\bigotimes_{s\in S}\mathrm{Unif}\{z\in\{0,1\}^{N_{n1s}}:\sum_i z_i=m_{n1s}\}\), and this conditional law is constant in the realized holdouts.

Conditional on the realized stage-1 recruitment history, \(\mathcal L((Z_{n2s})_{s:C_{n,s}(\rho)=1}\mid\mathcal F_{n,1}(\rho))=\bigotimes_{s:C_{n,s}(\rho)=1}\mathrm{Unif}\{z\in\{0,1\}^{N_{n2s}}:\sum_i z_i=m_{n2s}\}\), and no stage-2 assignment vector is generated when \(C_{n,s}(\rho)=0\).

Before stage-1 treatment assignment, \(\{H_{n,s}(\rho):s\in S\}\) is drawn independently of the fixed baseline array \(B\), independently across strata, and uniformly over subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,N_{n1s}\}\) of size \(\lfloor\rho N_{n1s}\rfloor\).

standard.name: independent stratified simple random sampling without replacement

assumptions.condition: \(H\) is nonempty and compact and satisfies \(H\subseteq[h_0,h_1]^S\) for fixed \(0<h_0\le h_1<\infty\).
For every \((k,s)\in K\times S\), \(N_{nks}/n\to r_{ks}\) uniformly with \(\min_{k,s}r_{ks}>0\).

For every \(n\), \(k\in K\), and \(s\in S\), writing \(\bar B_{nks}=N_{nks}^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{N_{nks}}B_{nksi}\), the empirical centered fourth moment satisfies \(N_{nks}^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{N_{nks}}(B_{nksi}-\bar B_{nks})^4\le M_4\).
The finite-population variances of \(B_{nksi}\) and \(U^0_{nksi}\) are eventually at least \(\epsilon\), uniformly over \((k,s)\in K\times S\).

Uniformly over \((k,s)\in K\times S\) and every \(u\) in the compact displacement window containing \(h_s\sqrt{r_{ks}}\) for \(h\in H\), \(N_{nks}^{-3/2}K_{nks}(u/\sqrt{N_{nks}})\to\lambda_{ks}u\), with \(0<\inf_{k,s}\lambda_{ks}\le\sup_{k,s}\lambda_{ks}<\infty\).

novel.justification: For each stage--stratum block, take a distribution on a bounded interval with continuously differentiable density \(f_{ks}\) satisfying \(0<\underline f\le f_{ks}\le\overline f<\infty\), and set \(B_{nksi}=F_{ks}^{-1}((i-1/2)/N_{nks})\). A uniform Riemann-sum calculation over every fixed compact displacement window gives \(N_{nks}^{-3/2}K_{nks}(u/\sqrt{N_{nks}})\to u\int f_{ks}(x)^2\,dx\). Thus the condition is realized by explicit bounded continuous-baseline quantile arrays, with \(\lambda_{ks}=\int f_{ks}^2\), and does not encode any holdout or weight conclusion.

assumptions.condition: The vector \( ((A_s)_{s\in S},(b_{1j},b_{2j},\kappa_j)_{j=(C,s)\in J},(c_s)_{s\in S})\) belongs to a fixed compact set every element of which is a joint limit, along one and the same baseline array \(B\), of the exact finite-array formulas displayed in the definitions of \(A_s\), \(b_{1j}\), \(b_{2j}\), and \(\kappa_j\).

novel.justification: Bounded continuous laws with outcome variance, local pair density, and mean--rank covariance bounded away from zero, including uniform laws and bounded two-component uniform mixtures, generate compact sets of these joint array limits. Requiring a single array to generate all coordinates excludes incompatible Gaussian tuples without stipulating any optimizer conclusion.

Fixed finite thresholds and bounded continuous baseline laws yield nonvanishing Gaussian probabilities for each prespecified complete signed recruitment cell. Trial protocols can omit cells whose design probability is below a declared operational minimum.

assumptions.condition: \(\sup_{\rho\in I,h\in H}\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{\min_{C:\exists s\,(C,s)\in J}p_{\mathrm{ref}}(n,C,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)<\epsilon\}\to0\text{ for each fixed admissible }B\).

novel.justification: For bounded continuous quantile arrays and fixed thresholds, the Fisher-completed candidate selector has a nondegenerate Gaussian limit conditionally on the realized data, so its complete-cell probabilities converge in probability to positive Gaussian cell probabilities.

assumptions.condition: The threshold vector \(c\) is fixed before treatment assignment and does not vary with \(n\).

definitions.name: Two-stage selective holdout design
definitions.construction: For \(\rho\in I\) and a fixed \(B_n\), construct \(Y^{(h)}\), draw the independent stratumwise holdouts, completely randomize stage 1 in both strata, observe \(Y^{\mathrm{obs},1}\), compute \(X_{n,s}(\rho)\), and realize \(C_n(\rho)\) and \(\mathcal F_{n,1}(\rho)\). Then recruit exactly the strata with \(C_{n,s}(\rho)=1\) and, conditional on that history, draw stage 2 independently by complete randomization only in those strata. This chronological construction is \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\).

definitions.name: Chronological local-alternative sampling law
definitions.construction: For each fixed \(B_n\), \(h\in H\cup\{0\}\), and \(\rho\in I\), generate outcomes from \(Y^{(h)}(0)=B\) and \(Y^{(h)}(1)=B+h_s/\sqrt n\), then execute \(\mathrm{def{:}sequential\mbox{-}design}\); the resulting probability kernel is \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\).

definitions.name: Dataset-specific Fisher sharp-null reference
definitions.construction: For each \(\rho\in I\) and dataset \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\) realized under \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\), form \(\widetilde Y^{0,\mathcal D(\rho)}\), enumerate \(\prod_{s\in S}\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)\), recompute \(X'_{n,s}\) and \(C'_n(\rho)\), retain exactly \(C'_n(\rho)=C_n(\rho)=C\), and then enumerate quota-respecting stage-2 assignments only in retained strata. This gives \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\), cell probability \(p_{\mathrm{ref}}(n,C,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\), normalized kernel \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,C}\), cdf \(F^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,j}(\cdot;\rho,\theta_j,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})\), and critical value \(q^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,j}(\rho,\theta_j,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})\).

definitions.name: Active-pair weighted selective randomization test
definitions.construction: For \(C=C_n(\rho)\) and active \(j=(C,s)\in J\) with \(C_s=1\), reject when \(T_j(\theta_j)\) exceeds the upper \(\alpha\)-critical value under \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,C}\), the data-dependent chronological Fisher reference supported exactly on \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\).

definitions.name: Full-cell exchangeable square-root selected Gaussian experiment
definitions.construction: For each fixed label \(C\), first draw the stage-1 Gaussian blocks independently across \(t\in S\): \(X_t\sim\mathcal N(A_t\sqrt{1-\rho}h_t,1)\), and for each active \(j=(C,s)\in J\), \((X_s,R_{1j})\) has correlation \(\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho}\) and mean \((A_s\sqrt{1-\rho}h_s,b_{1j}h_s)\). Realize the signed cell from the inequalities \(X_t>c_t\). Conditional on obtaining \(C\), draw \(R_{2j}\sim\mathcal N(b_{2j}h_s,1)\) independently across active strata and independently of all stage-1 blocks. Thus, for active \(j=(C,s)\), the chronological triple has covariance \(\begin{psmallmatrix}1&\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho}&0\\\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho}&1&0\\0&0&1\end{psmallmatrix}\), and its selected law is restricted and normalized to \(E_C=\bigcap_{t:C_t=1}\{X_t>c_t\}\cap\bigcap_{t:C_t=0}\{X_t\le c_t\}\).

definitions.name: Selected-score upper quantile
definitions.construction: For \(0\le r_{\mathrm g}<1\), \(q_{\beta}(r_{\mathrm g},x)\) is the unique \(q\) satisfying \(\Pr\{r_{\mathrm g}Z+\sqrt{1-r_{\mathrm g}^2}E>q\mid Z>x\}=\beta\) for independent standard normal \(Z,E\).

definitions.name: Selected-quantile chord equality
definitions.construction: For \(0<\beta<1\), \(0\le r<1\), \(c_0,c_1\in\mathbb R\), and \(0<t<1\), \(\operatorname{Eq}_{\beta,r}(c_0,c_1;t)\) is the predicate \(q_{\beta}(r,(1-t)c_0+tc_1)=(1-t)q_{\beta}(r,c_0)+tq_{\beta}(r,c_1)\).

definitions.name: Analytic branch and equality system
definitions.construction: Form all angular roots \(\partial_{\theta}\Pi_j=0\), angular multiple roots, angular endpoint transitions, reduced-factor projection endpoints, holdout stationary roots, multiple stationary roots, distinct-branch crossings, nontransverse crossings, candidate-value ties, flat-branch identities, and identical-branch identities on \(I\); retain every point, interval, and symbolic equality predicate generated by these systems.

definitions.name: Tolerance-certified optimizer handle
definitions.construction: Use outward-rounded Gaussian tail integration, monotone critical-value brackets, derivative-based oscillation bounds, and adaptive box subdivision of the compact \((\rho,\theta)\)-domain to enclose \(V^{\star}\) and the near-optimal design sets; an optional separation certificate consists of isolating boxes, interval root uniqueness tests, exclusions on their complements, strict candidate-value comparisons, and a positive objective gap outside the winning boxes.

definitions.name: Shrinking-margin transfer handle
definitions.construction: For each fixed baseline array \(B\), combine a joint permutation Berry--Esseen bound for selector, ranks, counts, and studentizers with a selected numerator--denominator ratio inequality and Gaussian anti-concentration to compare the cell margin \(m_n\) with the array-dependent error \(\eta_n(B)\).

statements.statement: Fix \(\rho\in I\), a realized dataset \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\), and \(C=C_n(\rho)\) with \(p_{\mathrm{ref}}(n,C,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)>0\). Under \(\widetilde Y^{0,\mathcal D(\rho)}\), every history in \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\) is imputable for \(X'\), \(C'\), \(R'_1\), \(R'_2\), and \(T'\). Conversely, every quota-respecting chronological holdout--assignment history on which these statistics are imputable and whose recomputed complete signed cell equals \(C\) belongs to \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\). Therefore this explicit support is exactly the same-cell imputability support, with no additional conditioning event.
statements.justification: The explicit support removes ambiguity about which histories are rerandomized and which quantities are recomputed after selection.
statements.gap: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao give the abstract conditional reference representation under imputability; this lemma identifies that support combinatorially for the present holdout and complete-cell design.
statements.consumer: Exact implementations can enumerate the reference law without an unspecified fiber or hidden conditioning restriction.

statements.statement: At the prespecified sharp-zero null \(h=0\), for every realized label \(C=C_n(\rho)\) with \(p_{\mathrm{ref}}(n,C,\mathcal D_n^{0,\rho},\rho)>0\) and every active \(j=(C,s)\in J\), the upper-rank selective randomization \(p\)-value from \(\mathrm{def{:}selective\mbox{-}test}\) is superuniform conditional on \(E_{n,C}(\rho)\) under \(\mathsf P_n^{0,\rho}\). Because \(Y^{(0)}(1)=Y^{(0)}(0)=B\), the conditional true chronological assignment law has exactly the support \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{0,\rho},\rho)\) and equals \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,C}\); summing its explicit product masses preserves level \(\alpha\).
statements.justification: This establishes finite-sample design-based validity on the same complete signed conditioning event used by every power theorem.
statements.gap: It specializes the exact conditioning argument of Freidling, Zhao, and Gao to the proposed threshold-and-holdout design; no novelty is claimed for validity alone.
statements.consumer: A trial team can deploy the optimized design without replacing exact sharp-null randomization inference by an asymptotic test.

statements.statement: Fix a complete label \(C\) represented in \(J\), and let \(j=(C,s)\in J\), so \(C_s=1\). Under \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\), the stratumwise holdout--stage-1 histories are independent, and each history-conditional stage-2 kernel is stratum-local and independent across retained strata. Thus, for measurable \(B_0\), \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{(X_{n,s},R_{1j},R_{2j})\in B_0,E_{n,C}(\rho)\}=\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{(X_{n,s},R_{1j},R_{2j})\in B_0,X_{n,s}>c_s\}\prod_{t\ne s}p_{nt}^{C_t}(1-p_{nt})^{1-C_t}\), where \(p_{nt}=\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{X_{n,t}>c_t\}\), and the same identity without \(B_0\) gives the cell probability. Under \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,\mathrm{base}}\), the product combinatorial mass on \(\prod_t\Omega_{n,1t}(\rho)\) and the stratum-local map \(X'_t\) give the same signed stage-1 factorization with \(p'_{nt}=\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,\mathrm{base}}\{X'_{n,t}>c_t\}\); after restriction to \(C'_n(\rho)=C\), the stage-2 part of \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,C}\) is an independent product over retained strata. The factorization holds likewise in \(\mathrm{def{:}gaussian\mbox{-}experiment}\). Division cancels every \(t\ne s\) signed factor under the sampling, explicit reference, and Gaussian laws, yielding exactly the displayed one-dimensional \(q_{\alpha,j}\) equation and \(\Pi_j\) integral.
statements.justification: This is the missing conditioning step that makes the one-dimensional selected-power formula valid for a complete two-stratum recruitment cell.
statements.gap: Existing selective-randomization validity conditions on the realized fiber, but the present analytic reduction additionally requires an explicit product cancellation for every positive and negative cell inequality.
statements.consumer: All holdout and weight calculations can use the scalar Gaussian integral without silently discarding the inactive stratum's selection inequality.

statements.statement: Write \(\bar B_{nks}=N_{nks}^{-1}\sum_iB_{nksi}\) and \(\bar U^0_{nks}=N_{nks}^{-1}\sum_iU^0_{nksi}\). Under the empirical centered fourth-moment bound, the variance margin, and positive shares, eventually and uniformly over the finite set \((k,s)\in K\times S\), \[\frac{\max_i(B_{nksi}-\bar B_{nks})^2}{\sum_i(B_{nksi}-\bar B_{nks})^2}\le\frac{\sqrt{M_4N_{nks}}}{(N_{nks}-1)\epsilon}\longrightarrow0.\] Because \(0\le U^0_{nksi}\le1\), the normalized centered midranks satisfy \[\frac{\max_i(U^0_{nksi}-\bar U^0_{nks})^2}{\sum_i(U^0_{nksi}-\bar U^0_{nks})^2}\le\frac{1}{(N_{nks}-1)\epsilon}\longrightarrow0.\] Hence both finite-population maximum-influence conditions required by the joint permutation approximation are consequences of the primitive class conditions rather than separate assumptions.
statements.justification: The finite-population Lindeberg ratios needed for transfer follow quantitatively from maintained moment, variance, and share conditions.
statements.gap: Finite-population central limit theorems commonly state maximum-influence as a premise; this lemma records the exact implication for centered outcomes and normalized midranks in the present class.
statements.consumer: The selected-transfer theorem no longer relies on a redundant regularity assumption that trial populations would have to verify separately.

statements.statement: For every active \(j\in J\), \(\rho\in I\), and \(\theta_j\in[0,\pi/2]\), the correlation definition and \(\lvert\kappa_j\rvert\le1\) give \[v_j(\rho,\theta_j)^2=1-\kappa_j^2(1-\rho)\cos^2(\theta_j)\ge\rho\ge\rho_0.\] This is a lower bound for the residual variance in the limiting selected Gaussian experiment; it does not assert a finite-\(n\) covariance bound.
statements.justification: Compact holdout support itself prevents degeneration of the Gaussian conditional residual scale.
statements.gap: The residual-scale margin is an algebraic consequence of the present square-root path and therefore should not be imposed as an independent positive-definiteness condition.
statements.consumer: All Gaussian quantile, branch, and certification bounds can use the declared design constant \(\rho_0\) directly.

statements.statement: For every fixed admissible baseline array \(B=(B_n)_n\), there is an array-dependent deterministic sequence \(\eta_n(B)\downarrow0\) with two separate conclusions. First, the sampling distance \(d_n^{\mathrm{samp}}(B)\), formed from the family of separately indexed laws \(\{\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}:\rho\in I,h\in H\}\), satisfies \(d_n^{\mathrm{samp}}(B)\le\eta_n(B)\); hence the sampling cdf conditional on \(E_{n,C}(\rho)\) converges to \(G_j^h(\cdot;\rho,\theta_j)\) uniformly over \(\rho\in I\), \(\theta\in[0,\pi/2]^J\), and \(h\in H\). Second, each \(\rho\)-indexed dataset \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\sim\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) generates its own completion, kernel, cdf \(F^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,j}(\cdot;\rho,\theta_j,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})\), critical value \(q^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,j}(\rho,\theta_j,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})\), and distance \(d_n^{\mathrm{ref}}(B,\rho,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})\), and \(\sup_{\rho\in I,\,h\in H}\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{d_n^{\mathrm{ref}}(B,\rho,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})>\eta_n(B)\}\to0\). Thus the random Fisher-reference cdf and critical value converge in their corresponding sampling probabilities to \(G_j^0(\cdot;\rho,\theta_j)\) and \(q_{\alpha,j}(\rho,\theta_j)\), uniformly in the displayed outer supremum. The permutation approximation uses the maximum-influence bounds derived in \(\mathrm{lem{:}derived\mbox{-}max\mbox{-}influence}\), while selected Gaussian ratio and anti-concentration bounds use the common lower margin \(\min\{\epsilon,\rho_0\}\) from the selection or variance premises and \(\mathrm{lem{:}derived\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}scale}\). After \(\mathrm{lem{:}full\mbox{-}cell\mbox{-}factorization}\), the rejection probability under each \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) converges uniformly to \(\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,h_s)\). No deterministic rate is asserted uniformly over all baseline arrays in \(\mathcal M\), and no finite-\(n\) covariance bound is inferred from the limiting \(\rho_0\) inequality.
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing bridge from exact full-cell finite-population conditioning to the scalar Gaussian design criterion.
statements.gap: Li--Ding and Shi--Ding control unconditional randomization statistics, while Tian--Taylor transfers iid laws through smooth randomized selection; none handles the complete signed cell, coupled without-replacement selector, random complement counts, studentization, imputed null reference, and moving selected quantile with one remainder.
statements.consumer: It turns analytic Gaussian holdout choices into uniformly valid asymptotic full-cell conditional-power statements for finite randomized enrichment trials.

statements.statement: For every \(0<\beta<1\) and \(0\le r<1\), the map \(x\mapsto q_{\beta}(r,x)\) is convex on \(\mathbb R\). Moreover, for every \(c_0,c_1\in\mathbb R\) and \(0<t<1\), \(\operatorname{Eq}_{\beta,r}(c_0,c_1;t)\) holds if and only if \(r=0\) or \(c_0=c_1\).
statements.justification: Convexity supplies the global single-crossing fact needed to optimize over arbitrary compact alternatives.
statements.gap: Shenfeld and van Handel prove Gaussian-measure convexity and equality cases but do not derive convexity of conditional selected-score quantiles.
statements.consumer: Power calculations need only the least clinically relevant effect coordinate, even when the prespecified alternative set is nonconvex.

statements.statement: For each active \(j=(C,s)\in J\), each fixed \( (\rho,\theta_j)\), and every \(u>\alpha\), \(\min_{h\in H}\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,h_s)\ge u\) if and only if \(\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,\ell_s)\ge u\), where \(\Pi_j\) is conditional on the complete signed event \(E_{n,C}(\rho)\). Hence the maximin value and every globally optimal design are unchanged when \(H\) is replaced by its least-coordinate vector \(\ell\).
statements.justification: This eliminates an infinite alternative-set optimization without imposing coordinatewise monotonicity below size.
statements.gap: No inspected enrichment or selective-inference result gives an exact above-size least-coordinate reduction for arbitrary compact positive alternatives.
statements.consumer: Designers can specify a clinically meaningful compact uncertainty set without introducing a numerical inner minimization.

statements.statement: Let \(\theta_{0j}=\arctan(b_{2j}/b_{1j})\). For the full-cell conditional power \(\Pi_j\), every maximizer of \(\theta_j\mapsto\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,\ell_s)\) lies in \( (\theta_{0j},\pi/2]\) when \(\Delta_j>0\), equals \(\theta_{0j}\) uniquely when \(\Delta_j=0\), and lies in \( (0,\theta_{0j})\) when \(\Delta_j<0\). These are exact equality strata for every active \(j=(C,s)\in J\).
statements.justification: The discrepancy index converts a two-dimensional weight search into a signed one-sided problem and identifies the proportional equality case.
statements.gap: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao suggest adaptive weighting, while Chen and Andrews study leftover Gaussian information; neither derives this primitive sign rule for enrichment holdouts.
statements.consumer: A trial designer obtains a falsifiable rule for whether stage 1 must receive more or less weight than the proportional-information benchmark.

statements.statement: Every jointly realizable continuous-rank primitive vector in \(\mathcal{M}\) satisfies \(A_s\kappa_j/b_{1j}\le5\sqrt{15}/18\), uniformly over active \(j=(C,s)\in J\).
statements.justification: This rules out a terminal pure-stage-2 plateau by linking Gaussian coordinates back to feasible finite populations.
statements.gap: The bound combines pair-spacing density, variance, and rank covariance and is not present in the Gaussian optimization literature.
statements.consumer: Endpoint optimality is certified over actual finite-population limits rather than an enlarged, potentially impossible Gaussian parameter box.

statements.statement: If \(\Delta_j\ge0\) for every active \(j=(C,s)\in J\), then \(\rho^{\star}=1-\rho_0\) is the unique maximizing holdout fraction for the full-cell conditional-power objective. At that fraction every binding cell has an optimal weight in \([\theta_{0j},\pi/2)\), with equality to \(\theta_{0j}\) exactly when \(\Delta_j=0\); slack-cell weights are the full superlevel sets required by \(\mathcal{S}^{\star}\).
statements.justification: This gives a closed-form and unique holdout decision on a nondegenerate primitive region.
statements.gap: Existing enrichment optimization gives numerical policies; no source derives a primitive sign condition forcing the maximal information-preserving holdout.
statements.consumer: A FOURIER-style design whose pilot primitives satisfy the sign certificate can choose the largest permitted holdout without global numerical search.

statements.statement: With \(M_4=2\) and \(\epsilon=1/100\), the baseline triangular array \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\), and \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) is its chronological local-alternative law. Its bounded symmetric supports give the empirical centered fourth-moment inequality in \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\mbox{-}fourth\mbox{-}moments}\). Substitution of its deterministic quantiles into the exact formulas for \(X\), \(R_1\), and \(R_2\) gives, for both active pairs \(j=((1,1),s)\), \(A_s=200\sqrt5/(53\sqrt{203})\), \(b_{1j}=8/5\), \(b_{2j}=43/100\), and \(\kappa_j=1393\sqrt5/(250\sqrt{203})\), with the certified enclosures in \(\mathrm{def{:}negative\mbox{-}mixture\mbox{-}witness}\) and \(\Delta_j\in[-0.80693126929013,-0.80693126929009]\). Uniformly over \(\rho\in I\) and \(h\in H\), the sampling probability of \(E_{n,(1,1)}(\rho)\) has limit inferior at least \(Q(-113/100)^2\in[0.75822626517532,0.75822626517534]\). Moreover, for every \(\delta>0\), \(\sup_{\rho\in I,h\in H}\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{\lvert p_{\mathrm{ref}}(n,(1,1),\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)-Q(-113/100)^2\rvert>\delta\}\to0\). Thus \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\) satisfies both the deterministic sampling margin and the random-reference margin.
statements.justification: This verifies joint finite-population realizability and exposes every numerical ingredient used by the interior certificate.
statements.gap: Gaussian-coordinate counterexamples alone need not correspond to any randomized finite population; this proposition realizes the signed regime with exact bounded distributions and certified primitive boxes.
statements.consumer: A referee can reproduce the negative-discrepancy example from its mixture weights, supports, allocation, and exact radical primitives.

statements.statement: Under the shifted sampling limit of \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) and the separate zero-drift critical-value limit of \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,C}\), for the explicit symmetric population \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\), the active set is \(J=\{((1,1),1),((1,1),2)\}\), both discrepancies are negative, and the rational interior design \( (\rho,\theta_1,\theta_2)=(5034/10000,25363/100000,25363/100000)\) has worst-cell power conditional on the complete both-selected event greater than \(0.86428621266\). Every admissible weight vector at \(\rho=0.02\) has worst-cell conditional power below \(0.86304573855\), and every admissible weight vector at \(\rho=0.98\) has worst-cell conditional power below \(0.86241162520\). Therefore every global maximizing holdout fraction is strictly interior.
statements.justification: The certified, fully specified witness shows that the endpoint theorem has a substantive opposite regime rather than being a universal monotonicity result.
statements.gap: No inspected paper gives a rigorously enclosed interior optimum for full-cell selective-randomization holdout power.
statements.consumer: Designers are warned that maximizing the holdout can lose power when selector drift is weak relative to mean--rank dependence.

statements.statement: On every primitive stratum defined by \(\mathrm{def{:}branch\mbox{-}system}\), each active cell's complete-event conditional envelope \(M_j\) and the global envelope \(F\) are finite maxima and minima of analytic or Puiseux-continuable branches. The global maximizing holdout set consists exactly of the retained interval endpoints, projected branch endpoints, stationary branch roots, branch intersections, and flat maximizing intervals attaining \(V^{\star}\); for each such \(\rho\), the full weight set is \(\prod_{j=(C,s)\in J}\{\theta_j:\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,\ell_s)\ge V^{\star}\}\). This characterization is necessary and sufficient in all positive, negative, zero, and mixed-sign \(\Delta\) regimes, with every \(\Pi_j\) conditioned on \(E_{n,C}(\rho)\).
statements.justification: This supplies the complete mixed-sign analytic geometry and preserves all ties and slack-cell weight continua.
statements.gap: Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu optimize a discretized policy program and do not characterize the continuous holdout argmax correspondence or its equality strata.
statements.consumer: The complete candidate list supports auditable global design optimization even when the optimizer is nonunique or lies on a branch transition.

statements.statement: For rational or algebraic primitive inputs, finite unions of closed rational intervals presenting each projected alternative coordinate, and every rational tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), the handle in \(\mathrm{def{:}tolerance\mbox{-}handle}\) terminates with an interval of width at most \(\varepsilon\) containing the full-cell conditional value \(V^{\star}\), a finite outer union containing \(\mathcal{S}^{\star}\) and contained in the \(2\varepsilon\)-power superlevel set, and a finite inner union contained in the \(\varepsilon\)-power superlevel set. It asserts a unique design only when the supplied separation certificate proves uniqueness against every retained competing branch and slack-cell weight set.
statements.justification: The computational statement is strong enough for design use but never asks an interval routine to decide equality of arbitrary exact real values.
statements.gap: Published enrichment optimizers report numerical solutions without a theorem enclosing the full optimizer set across equality strata.
statements.consumer: A protocol can archive machine-checkable value and design boxes and reserve point recommendations for explicitly separated cases.

statements.statement: If \(\Delta_j=0\) for every active cell and the two active full-cell conditional problems have identical primitives, then, under the complete signed-cell conditional law, every cell's unique individually optimal weight is \(\theta_{0j}=\arctan(b_{2j}/b_{1j})\), the two cell envelopes coincide, and the unique holdout fraction is \(1-\rho_0\).
statements.justification: This is the required reduction to proportional Gaussian information weighting.
statements.gap: It is a sanity-check corollary rather than an independent novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It lets implementers validate the general optimizer against a closed-form symmetric benchmark.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathrm{def{:}shrinking\mbox{-}margin\mbox{-}handle}\), characterize the sharp rate frontier for cell-probability or score-boundary margins \(m_n\downarrow0\): for each admissible baseline array \(B\), determine necessary and sufficient relations between \(m_n\) and \(\eta_n(B)\) for conditional sampling-cdf, data-dependent zero-null reference-cdf, quantile, and local-power transfer, and construct a finite-population sequence showing failure below that frontier.
statements.justification: The fixed positive-margin theorem leaves the scientifically relevant boundary where recruitment cells become rare or rankings unstable.
statements.gap: Tian and Taylor require selection-likelihood control, while available post-selection nonuniformity results do not identify the without-replacement enrichment boundary.
statements.consumer: The frontier would tell trial planners how close a recruitment threshold may approach an estimated score boundary before Gaussian power calculations cease to be reliable.

sampling_model.design: For each \(\rho\in I\), the chronological two-stage adaptive enrichment law \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) fixes \(B_n\), forms \(Y^{(h)}(0)=B\) and \(Y^{(h)}(1)=B+h_s/\sqrt n\), draws independent stratumwise simple-random holdouts of the \(\rho\)-specified sizes, completely randomizes stage 1, realizes the complete signed recruitment cell, and only then completely randomizes stage 2 within recruited strata conditional on the history. The resulting dataset is \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\). Its Fisher reference uses the same \(\rho\), enumerates the exact candidate support \(\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)\), recomputes the selector and complete cell under the sharp-zero completion, retains exactly the observed cell, and then enumerates stage-2 assignments only in retained strata. Its cell probability, kernel, cdf, critical value, and reference distance are all indexed by that design value and realized dataset.
sampling_model.units: A fixed baseline finite-population triangular array in two strata and two stages; under \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\), the only randomness is the holdout and chronological treatment assignment.
sampling_model.treatment: Balanced binary treatment is completely randomized in every stage-1 stratum and, after recruitment, in each selected stage-2 stratum under its history-conditional kernel.
sampling_model.overlap: Both treatment arms have positive limiting shares, every complete signed cell represented in the active index set has probability at least \(\epsilon\), and the limiting selected Gaussian residual variance satisfies \(v_j(\rho,\theta_j)^2\ge\rho\ge\rho_0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The exact complement Neyman studentizer, normalized-midrank permutation studentizers, random complement counts, pair-spacing slopes, and mean--rank correlations are embedded jointly in the finite-population transfer. Maximum-influence ratios are derived from the empirical centered fourth-moment bound, finite-population variance margin, and positive shares; no oracle nuisance quantity or separate Lindeberg premise is assumed.

tldr: For a two-stratum, two-stage enrichment experiment, fix a baseline array \(B_n\) and generate local alternatives by \(Y^{(h)}(0)=B\) and \(Y^{(h)}(1)=B+h_s/\sqrt n\). Each holdout value \(\rho\) defines its own chronological sampling law \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\), realized dataset \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\), and same-design Fisher sharp-null reference. The reference enumerates all quota-respecting holdout--assignment pairs, recomputes the selector from completed outcomes, retains exactly the observed complete signed cell, then randomizes stage 2 only in retained strata; its support and cell probability are explicit. For every admissible baseline array, an array-dependent remainder separately transfers the sampling cdf to the shifted Gaussian law and the indexed random reference cdf to its zero-drift law. The finite-population maximum-influence ratios are derived from the empirical centered fourth-moment bound, variance margin, and positive shares, while the limiting Gaussian residual variance is bounded below by \(\rho_0\) from the holdout design itself. Cross-stratum factorization reduces both limits to scalar critical-value and power integrals. Selected-score quantiles are convex, with chord equality exactly when the correlation is zero or the chord endpoints coincide, and reduce every compact positive alternative set to its least coordinate. The sign of \(\Delta_j=A_s-\kappa_jb_{1j}\) determines the weight side; nonnegative discrepancies force the largest holdout, an explicit two-component uniform mixture verifies both sampling and random-reference margins and yields a certified interior regime, and mixed signs admit an equality-aware analytic optimizer correspondence with tolerance-certified boxes.

project_justification.gap: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao establish exact selective randomization inference and explicitly leave holdout allocation and powerful selection-dependent statistics open. Existing finite-population central limit theorems are unconditional, selective central limit theorems use independent sampling with smooth external randomization, and enrichment-design optimization uses model-based numerical programs. None supplies a design-uniform, array-specific without-replacement transfer that separates the shifted sampling law from the dataset-dependent Fisher reference, or an analytic holdout--weight power frontier.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a design-based maximin conditional-local-power problem in which the holdout fraction changes both the selection law and the amount of stage-1 randomization information retained for exact testing. Its optimizer may be an endpoint, an interior point, or a set-valued mixed-sign correspondence, so neither heuristic weight choice nor a floating-point optimizer resolves the design question.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the complete signed-cell selected Gaussian limit from a fixed baseline array and the separately indexed local-alternative laws \(\{\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}:\rho\in I,h\in H\}\). For each \(\rho\), it constructs from \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\) the same-design Fisher completion and the exact finite support of quota-respecting candidate histories, recomputes selection for every candidate, retains exactly the observed complete cell, and integrates the ensuing stage-2 kernels. The reference cell probability is an explicit combinatorial sum. A deterministic sampling-cell margin is separated from a random-reference margin stated uniformly in probability. For each admissible baseline array, one common array-dependent modulus controls the sampling-cdf family uniformly over design and alternatives and controls the reference family through an outer supremum of the corresponding sampling probabilities. The required finite-population maximum-influence ratios follow from explicit inequalities using \(M_4\), \(\epsilon\), and positive block shares, and the limiting Gaussian residual variance obeys \(v_j^2\ge\rho\ge\rho_0\); neither is imposed separately. Cross-stratum factorization then yields the scalar selected integrals, which are solved through selected-quantile convexity with the exact chord-equality predicate, inverse-Mills factorization, realizability inequalities, analytic branch exhaustion, and certificate-aware interval computation. The newly maintained pair-spacing condition is realized directly by bounded continuous-density quantile arrays. The negative-discrepancy regime is anchored by deterministic quantiles from an explicit two-component uniform mixture with stated weights, supports, stratum allocations, exact primitive limits, reference-margin convergence, and certified enclosures.

related_work: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao's Proposition 1 gives superuniform selective validity and type-I control, Proposition 2 gives the conditional reference representation and its computability under imputability, and Section 5 motivates holdout and statistic design in two-stage enrichment. The exact candidate-history support here specializes that representation by enumerating every quota-respecting holdout--assignment pair, recomputing the complete cell, and integrating only the stage-2 kernels for retained strata. The asymptotic statement separately transfers the shifted sampling cdf under \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) and the data-dependent Fisher-reference cdf under \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,C}\), with distinct sampling and random-reference margins. Li and Ding provide the vector finite-population central limit theorem used to embed assignment contrasts, and Shi and Ding provide quantitative permutation-approximation and variance-estimation ingredients. In the present class, their maximum-influence premise is verified by explicit centered-outcome and normalized-midrank bounds rather than separately assumed. Tian and Taylor supply the conditional likelihood-transfer architecture in an iid randomized-selection model; the needed limiting residual-scale bound here instead follows algebraically from \(\rho\ge\rho_0\) and \(\lvert\kappa_j\rvert\le1\). Shenfeld and van Handel supply the Ehrhard--Borell machinery from which selected-quantile convexity and its chord-equality classification are derived. Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu provide the nearest two-stage enrichment optimization benchmark, but their sparse program targets model-based operating characteristics rather than exact full-cell conditional-randomization local power. Chen and Andrews characterize optimal conditional inference in parametric Gaussian adaptive experiments; the present design problem instead uses fixed baseline populations and without-replacement assignment. Thall's review confirms that subgroup selection, trial utility, and inferential quality remain distinct design axes.
technical_internal_limitation: The central proof risk is the per-array common transfer in \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}selected\mbox{-}transfer}\). For every design value \(\rho\), the true experiment fixes \(B_n\), uses \(Y^{(h)}(0)=B\) and \(Y^{(h)}(1)=B+h_s/\sqrt n\), and samples under its separately indexed law \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\); it never treats a positive local alternative as satisfying the sharp null. Each \(\rho\)-indexed dataset induces its own Fisher completion and explicit same-cell candidate-history support \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\), with no further imputability event. Uniformity in \(\rho\) is asserted only through outer probabilities under the corresponding laws. The sampling-cell margin is deterministic, whereas the reference-cell margin is convergence in probability of the random combinatorial probability \(p_{\mathrm{ref}}\). The scalar formulas are licensed only after cross-stratum factorization under the sampling, explicit reference, and Gaussian laws. The maximum-influence step is settled by \(\mathrm{lem{:}derived\mbox{-}max\mbox{-}influence}\): the centered baseline ratio is at most \(\sqrt{M_4N_{nks}}/((N_{nks}-1)\epsilon)\), and the centered-midrank ratio is at most \(1/((N_{nks}-1)\epsilon)\). The Gaussian residual variance is at least \(\rho_0\) by \(\mathrm{lem{:}derived\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}scale}\), but that limiting identity is not used as a finite-\(n\) covariance bound. The remaining proof must control hypergeometric complement counts, both studentizers, local rank drift under the newly maintained pair-spacing condition, null imputation, conditional cdfs, and moving quantiles with \(\eta_n(B)\), uniformly over \(\rho\), \(\theta\), and \(h\) for each fixed admissible baseline array, using \(\min\{\epsilon,\rho_0\}\) when a common variance, selection, and residual-scale margin is required. No deterministic rate uniform over the qualitative class \(\mathcal M\) is claimed. The early kill test is the two-law transfer and reference-margin verification for the explicit bounded nonproportional mixture family.
honest_scope: Finite-sample exactness is asserted only at the prespecified Fisher sharp-zero null \(h=0\). Positive local alternatives are sampled from \(Y^{(h)}\) under the separately indexed law \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\); for every \(\rho\), the realized dataset defines a separate same-design completion and an explicit candidate-history support obtained by recomputing the selector and retaining exactly the observed complete cell. No unspecified imputability fiber is conditioned upon. Uniform-in-\(\rho\) reference transfer means an outer supremum of the corresponding \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\)-probabilities. The sampling-cell margin is deterministic; the random reference-cell margin is a separate convergence-in-probability condition, verified for \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\). The sampling cdf converges to a shifted selected Gaussian law, whereas each data-dependent reference cdf converges in its corresponding sampling probability to the zero-drift law. For each admissible \(B\), the same array-dependent \(\eta_n(B)\) is uniform over holdouts, weights, and compact local alternatives, but no rate is uniform over all of \(\mathcal M\). Maximum influence is derived from the empirical centered fourth-moment bound, the finite-population variance margin, and positive shares. The bound \(v_j^2\ge\rho_0\) concerns the limiting Gaussian residual only and supplies no finite-\(n\) covariance assertion. Whenever the proof needs one common lower constant across maintained finite-population margins and this limiting residual bound, it uses \(\min\{\epsilon,\rho_0\}\). The scalar formulas apply only to active \(j=(C,s)\) with \(C_s=1\) after complete-cell product cancellation. The pair-spacing condition is a newly maintained primitive condition realized by bounded continuous-density quantile arrays. The selected-quantile chord equality is exactly \(\operatorname{Eq}_{\beta,r}(c_0,c_1;t)\), classified by \(r=0\) or \(c_0=c_1\). The mixture certificate separates both holdout endpoints without asserting a unique interior optimizer; general computation remains set-valued unless a separation certificate proves uniqueness. Binary outcomes, nonzero sharp-null inversion, weak average-effect nulls, deterministic outcome-dependent splits, and continuous-biomarker cutoffs remain outside scope.

novelty_justification: The closest result is Freidling, Zhao, and Gao's exact selective randomization test: Proposition 1 gives selective type-I control, Proposition 2 gives the conditional reference representation and computability under imputability, and Section 5 poses holdout and statistic design. The closest design comparator is Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu's sparse-program optimization, which is model-based, discretized, and targeted to expected sample size and familywise error rather than conditional randomization-power geometry. The kernel separates the fixed baseline array, the family of true local-alternative sampling laws \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\), and, for each \(\rho\)-indexed dataset, its exact combinatorial candidate support, recomputed complete-cell selector, Fisher reference, cell probability, cdf, critical value, and distance. A deterministic sampling margin and a random-reference convergence-in-probability margin license separate shifted-sampling and zero-drift-reference transfers; explicit inequalities derive both centered-outcome and normalized-midrank maximum-influence ratios, and the holdout restriction derives the limiting residual bound \(v_j^2\ge\rho_0\), without adding conclusion-shaped assumptions. Cross-stratum product cancellation then yields the scalar selected-power functional. Within that justified limit experiment, selected-quantile convexity has the explicit chord-equality classification \(\operatorname{Eq}_{\beta,r}(c_0,c_1;t)\iff(r=0\text{ or }c_0=c_1)\), arbitrary compact alternatives reduce to least coordinates, \(\Delta_j\) determines the admissible weight side, nonnegative discrepancies force the largest holdout, an explicit bounded mixture verifies the reference margin and realizes a certified negative-discrepancy interior regime, and mixed signs admit a complete equality-aware analytic argmax correspondence.
